content.introduction: According to the latest data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the US annual inflation rate was 3.4% for the 12 months ending in August 2026, which remained unchanged from July. However, by September 2026, the annual inflation rate had increased to 3.7%, driven by higher energy prices. Specifically, gasoline prices rose 34.2% year-over-year, and fuel oil prices increased 74.2%. Core inflation, excluding food and energy, stood at 2.4% for the 12 months through August 2026.
body:
The latest U.S. inflation figures show that consumer prices continued to rise in August 2026. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 0.4% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis. Over the 12 months through August, overall consumer prices increased 3.4%. This annual inflation rate was unchanged from July, meaning inflation remained at the same yearly pace even though prices moved higher during the month. [...] The August 2026 CPI report was released on September 11, 2026. The next U.S. CPI report, covering September 2026, is scheduled for October 14, 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. [...] For now, the latest data show a 3.4% annual headline inflation rate, while core inflation stands at 2.4%. Future reports will help show whether price pressures continue at a similar pace or begin moving higher or lower. Consumers, businesses, and policymakers will continue watching categories such as energy, shelter, food, and other services to understand how the inflation picture develops through the remainder of 2026.

## The US annual inflation rate accelerated to 3.7% in September 2026, up from 3.4% in each of the previous two months and above market expectations of 3.6%, driven by higher energy prices. Gasoline rose 34.2% yoy, more than 27.4% in August and fuel oil prices increased 74.2%, compared with 52% previously. Inflation also accelerated for shelter, to 3.2% from 3%, but slowed for food to 2.5% from 2.7%.
